Market analysis: specialty coffee shop in Austin, TX
Copy as text

This section summarizes public demographic evidence for opening your specialty coffee shop in Austin, TX, compared with Nashville, TN and Charlotte, NC. It is written so it can be adapted for the market analysis section of a business plan.

Market size and growth

Austin, TX has an estimated population of 979,539. Population grew 3% between the 2019 and 2024 ACS 5-year estimates, indicating an expanding resident base. Of the 3 locations evaluated, it has the lowest five-year growth rate.

Household purchasing power

Median household income in Austin, TX is $93,658. That is the highest of the 3 locations evaluated (Nashville, TN: $77,371; Charlotte, NC: $82,068). Household income indicates how much local residents may be able to spend; it does not measure demand for your specialty coffee shop.

Property cost context

The median home value in Austin, TX is $555,300, the highest of the 3 locations. Home values are a rough signal of local property costs, not commercial rents; occupancy costs for your specialty coffee shop need to be confirmed with lease quotes for the specific site.

Comparative position

Compared with Nashville, TN and Charlotte, NC, Austin, TX leads on household income and population but trails on population growth.

Population
1	Austin, TX	979,539
2	Charlotte, NC	903,844
3	Nashville, TN	690,130
Median household income
1	Austin, TX	$93,658
2	Charlotte, NC	$82,068
3	Nashville, TN	$77,371
Median home value
1	Austin, TX	$555,300
2	Nashville, TN	$413,600
3	Charlotte, NC	$385,700
5-year population change
1	Charlotte, NC	5.4%
2	Nashville, TN	4%
3	Austin, TX	3%
Further research before committing
Count existing specialty coffee shop competitors serving the same customers in your intended trade area, and note their pricing and positioning.
Obtain two or three commercial lease quotes for suitable sites in Austin, TX to replace home values with real occupancy costs.
Gather direct demand evidence for your specialty coffee shop: customer interviews, pre-orders, a waitlist, or foot-traffic counts at candidate sites.
Sources
U.S. Census Bureau. American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates, 2020–2024: total population (B01003), median household income in 2024 inflation-adjusted dollars (B19013), median home value (B25077). Retrieved 2026-10-11 from https://api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs5.
U.S. Census Bureau. American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates, 2015–2019: total population (B01003). Retrieved 2026-10-11 from https://api.census.gov/data/2019/acs/acs5.

DECISION REPORT · SAMPLE

Should I open my specialty coffee shop in Austin, or in Nashville or Charlotte?

Specialty coffee shop · Austin, TX

SAMPLE · LIVE DATA
October 11, 2026

WHAT THE FIGURES SHOW

Austin, TX has higher median household income, population and median home value than both Nashville, TN and Charlotte, NC, and lower 5-year population change than both. One gap is small and may not be real: 5-year population change against Nashville, TN (1 point).

These figures describe the people who live in each place. They do not measure demand for your business, competitors, rent or foot traffic, so on their own they cannot recommend a location.

Sources cited
4 of 4 key figures
Each links to its official table. This counts citations; it is not a measure of how certain the findings are.
Median household income
$93,658: $16,287 (21%) higher than Nashville, TN ($77,371); $11,590 (14%) higher than Charlotte, NC ($82,068).
Population
979,539: 289,409 (42%) higher than Nashville, TN (690,130); 75,695 (8.4%) higher than Charlotte, NC (903,844).
5-year population change
3%: 1 point lower than Nashville, TN (4%), a small gap that may not be real; 2.4 points lower than Charlotte, NC (5.4%).
Median home value
$555,300: $141,700 (34%) higher than Nashville, TN ($413,600); $169,600 (44%) higher than Charlotte, NC ($385,700).

None of these differences has been tested for statistical significance. Census figures are survey estimates with margins of error, which this report does not show yet and which are wider for smaller places. Gaps under 5% (or under 2 points for population change) are flagged as small because survey error alone often produces gaps that size. The flag is a reading aid, not a test: a larger gap can also fall within the error, especially for smaller places.
